lyrics:
[Intro: chiming delay guitar, soft pulsing bass]

[Verse 1: male tenor, hushed, expectant]
I've got a sign with your name, I made it twice
My hands were shaking and it didn't look right
We've talked for years, I know your voice
I've never seen your face. I never had the choice.

[Pre-Chorus: drums enter]
Everybody's pouring through the sliding doors
Running into arms, dropping bags on the floor

[Chorus: wide, soaring, full band]
And I'm standing at the arrivals gate
Heart in my throat, I can hardly wait
Will I run, will I freeze, will I fall on my face?
How will I know you in a crowded place?
I've loved you my whole life, sight unseen
I'm standing at the arrivals gate

[Verse 2: voice close, the turn]
But that's backwards. I'm the one coming in
Off a long, long flight, with the shape I'm in
And you're the one at the rail with the sign
You've had my name on it since before time

[Pre-Chorus: drums build]
And I'll know you, I'll know you, there's no mistake
By the scars in the hands reaching over the gate

[Chorus: wide, soaring, full band]
And you're standing at the arrivals gate
Arms out wide, you could hardly wait
I will run, I will freeze, I will fall on my face
You'll pick me out of any crowded place
You've loved me my whole life, and you've seen
Jesus, at the arrivals gate

[Bridge: half-time, guitars ringing]
No more goodbyes in that terminal
No lost and found, no last call
Every tear wiped by the hand that made the eye
Home. Home. I'm home.

[Final Chorus: full band, highest]
And you're standing at the arrivals gate
Arms out wide, you could hardly wait
I will run, I will freeze, I will fall on my face
You'll pick me out of any crowded place
You've loved me my whole life, and you've seen
Jesus, at the arrivals gate

[Outro: delay guitar, a crowd murmuring, one voice]
There you are.
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 112 BPM, 4/4, D major. A steady, widening anthem that starts hushed and opens like doors.

VOICE: Male tenor, clear and earnest. Nearly whispered in verse 1, lifting to a long, open, held melody in the choruses. Verse 2 is sung as if he has just understood something. One spoken phrase at the end, in a different, calm voice.

INSTRUMENTS: An electric guitar with dotted-eighth delay playing chiming patterns, a pulsing eighth-note bass, steady drums with a big open snare from the pre-chorus, a second guitar with shimmer, piano, a string pad, airport crowd sound at the end.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, delay guitar. 0:14 Verse 1. 0:40 Pre-chorus. 0:50 Chorus 1. 1:22 Verse 2, 'that's backwards'. 1:46 Pre-chorus, the scars. 1:56 Chorus 2. 2:28 Bridge, half-time. 2:56 Final chorus. 3:28 Outro, crowd murmur and 'There you are' at 3:42.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Stadium rock in the 1980s-to-2000s tradition of ringing delay guitars: wide, bright, emotional, drums roomy.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'But that's backwards' at 1:22, when the whole picture turns round.

THE REVEAL: Verse 1 and the first chorus are a man at an airport. At 1:22 he sees that he is the one arriving, and at 1:50 he says how he will recognise who is waiting. The second chorus keeps the tune and changes every pronoun.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Nervous, longing, turned around, home.
